name: write_logic
summary: Write one logic value to a device, by logic type name or number, as a chip or console would. Answers the value read back at once.

help.text: Returns requested_value, previous_value and current_value. current_value is read back at once and can differ from the request: the device clamps it (On 7 reads 1), ignores it (a colour index only paint sets), or moves toward it over time (a solar panel turning). The write still succeeds. A write that opens a vent, valve, pump or regulator (On or Open from 0 to 1, a vent's Mode from inward to outward, a turbo pump's Mode turned the other way, a volume pump's Setting from 0) first runs the write lint rules on the pipe networks it opens to, as they stand at the write, every time (see lint). A problem refuses the write as lint_refused (its data lists each rule, message and thing) unless allow_lint; a warning comes back in warnings [{code, message, index, reference_id}], absent when there are none. A write that opens nothing runs no rule. A report (dry_run) answers {report_only, problems, gateway_id, reference_id, logic_type, requested_value, previous_value (the device's value before the write), opens, warnings} and writes nothing (see report_only).

logic_type.description: A logic type name (Temperature) or number.

value.description: The value to write: a finite number.

allow_lint.description: Default false: a write that opens a device onto a network a write lint rule finds a problem on is refused (lint_refused); true writes, each problem a warning.

dry_run.description: Default false. true checks the write, the write lint rules included, and writes nothing; the reply starts report_only (see report_only).
